A tournament on the local network shows as one in Browse servers: its matches go under Ongoing Tournament (also on the Local tab, above the other local servers) - on the public list only an official server's tournament does, so nobody can dress up a server as one. A tournament match reports its players in the heartbeat as how many of its roster are in the game out of how many it waits for (2/2, 1/2, 0/2) - not its slots with the bots warming it up and the casters (it showed 6/22 for a 1v1).

Docker image released with every version tag: pushing a tag (e.g. 4.2.0) builds ghcr.io/teamhypersomnia/hypersomnia-server:<tag> and :latest. The image takes builds/latest from hypersomnia.io, which changes only when a build is deployed - so the job waits for the headless build of the tagged commit, then until the deployed AppImage is byte for byte that build, checks the version inside the image before anything is pushed, and signs it with cosign. Before, the image was built on every push to master, right after the build and before the deploy: it always held the previous release (latest had 4.1.0 after 4.2.0). Also runnable by hand with a tag.

README_SERVER.md rewritten as the specification of hosting a server, shown at hypersomnia.io/host: the steps themselves are now the config generator's (hypersomnia.io/generator), this page explains the rest - ports, updates, tournaments, admins, configuration, environment variables, several servers, the server key, troubleshooting, command line flags. It describes the planned behavior that the game does not have yet: an environment variable for every setting (HYPERSOMNIA_SERVER_NAME, _MAP_CYCLE, _ADMINS, _PASSWORD, _SLOTS, _SERVER_INSTANCES, _PORT, _WEB_PORT, _BROWSER_PLAYERS, _DAILY_UPDATE, _TIME_ZONE, _DISCORD_WEBHOOK), tournaments only by environment variables or flags (--tournament, --tournament-team-size, --tournament-teams, --tournament-arenas) with an open first round of "Match #N (any pair)" servers, community arenas downloaded when first needed. Screenshots of Browse servers in docs/images: a community server, and a LAN tournament's matches named by their teams and open to any pair.
